title: Samsung Healthcare HM70A Ultrasound System - Probe Not Recognized or Port Damage
description: Troubleshooting when the HM70A does not recognize a probe or shows intermittent connection due to probe, cable, or port-related issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the ultrasound system from active patient use if imaging is required. Move the patient to a functioning system before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Connect the probe and power on the system. Observe for “Probe not recognized” message, no image display, or intermittent connection when moving cable.

steps.title: Check Probe Connection (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect the probe to the port. Ensure connector is fully seated and locking mechanism (if present) is engaged.

steps.title: Inspect Probe Connector Pins
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the probe connector for bent or missing pins, contamination (gel, dust, debris), or corrosion.

steps.title: Inspect System Port for Damage
steps.instructions: Use a flashlight to inspect the port for bent or recessed pins, debris, or physical damage.

steps.title: Clean Connector and Port (If Needed)
steps.instructions: Use approved cleaning methods if contamination is present. Do not insert anything that could damage pins.

steps.title: Test with a Known-Good Probe
steps.instructions: Connect a different compatible probe to determine if the issue is probe-related or system-related.

steps.title: Test the Suspect Probe on Another System (If Available)
steps.instructions: Connect the original probe to another compatible ultrasound system to confirm whether the probe is defective.

steps.title: Check for Intermittent Connection
steps.instructions: Gently move the probe cable near the connector while observing system response.

steps.title: Reboot the System
steps.instructions: Power the system off, wait 15–30 seconds, and restart to clear temporary communication faults.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound probe not recognized on Samsung HM70A; no image displayed.
CCR.Cause: Damaged probe connector pins causing loss of communication with system.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defective probe from service and replaced with known-good probe; confirmed normal operation.

helpfulDetails: Presence of bent pins or debris

title: Samsung Healthcare HM70A Ultrasound System - Image Dropout or Quality Degradation
description: Troubleshooting intermittent or poor ultrasound image quality caused by probe, connection, or system setting issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Move the patient to another functioning ultrasound system before troubleshooting if imaging is critical.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the system and determine if the issue is complete or partial dropout, intermittent or constant, and if it affects specific probes or all probes.

steps.title: Check Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Reconnect the probe securely and inspect for loose connection, bent pins, or debris in the port.

steps.title: Test with a Known Good Probe
steps.instructions: Use a different probe to determine if the issue is probe-related or system-related.

steps.title: Inspect the Probe Cable
steps.instructions: Check for physical damage and observe for image flickering when moving the cable.

steps.title: Check Imaging Settings
steps.instructions: Verify gain, depth, and frequency settings and reset to default presets if needed.

steps.title: Check for Overheating
steps.instructions: Assess system temperature and fan operation, especially after prolonged use.

steps.title: Inspect Probe Port
steps.instructions: Look for bent pins, loose connectors, or physical damage in the probe port.

steps.title: Perform a System Reboot
steps.instructions: Restart the system to clear temporary software or processing issues.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound image intermittently dropping out during use on Samsung HM70A.
CCR.Cause: Faulty linear probe cable causing intermittent signal loss when manipulated.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced defective probe with known good unit; verified normal image quality restored.

helpfulDetails: Alarm or error behavior during imaging
Environmental factors such as heat or extended use

title: Samsung Healthcare HM70A Ultrasound System - System Fails to Boot or Crashes
description: Troubleshooting boot failures, crashes, or restart issues caused by power, accessories, or system faults.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the system from clinical use if it is unreliable. Move the patient to another ultrasound system before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify Power Source and AC Adapter
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is plugged into a known-good outlet. Check the AC adapter for secure connection, indicator lights, and damage.

steps.title: Check Battery Status (If Equipped)
steps.instructions: Disconnect AC power and attempt to power on using battery only. Then reconnect AC and observe charging indicators.

steps.title: Perform a Full Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Shut down the system completely. Disconnect AC power and remove battery if accessible. Hold the power button for 10–15 seconds, then reconnect power and restart.

steps.title: Disconnect All External Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove all probes and USB/network devices and attempt to boot the system with no peripherals connected.

steps.title: Test with Known-Good Probe (After Boot)
steps.instructions: If the system boots without accessories, reconnect one known-good probe to verify stability.

steps.title: Observe Boot Behavior and Error Messages
steps.instructions: Identify whether the system shows no display, freezes on logo, reboots repeatedly, or displays error messages.

steps.title: Check for Overheating or Environmental Issues
steps.instructions: Ensure vents are not blocked and check for excessive heat, dust buildup, or abnormal fan noise.

steps.title: Attempt Safe Restart / Software Recovery (If Available)
steps.instructions: Use system recovery or safe startup mode per facility protocol if accessible.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound system would not boot and intermittently restarted during use.
CCR.Cause: System failed to boot with accessories connected; issue isolated after removing faulty probe.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defective probe from service; system booted normally and returned to operation.

helpfulDetails: Presence of heat, noise, or fan issues
Final system status (working or sent for repair)

title: Samsung Healthcare HM70A Ultrasound System - DICOM or Network Export Failure
description: Failure to send images to PACS, DICOM transfer errors, network disconnects, or studies not appearing in the archive.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay patient care while troubleshooting. Use an alternate ultrasound system if image export is required immediately.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to send a test image or study to PACS. Observe error messages, send failed or timeout messages, and lack of confirmation.

steps.title: Check Network Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect Ethernet cable at system and wall port. Ensure it is fully seated and check for link/activity lights.

steps.title: Verify Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Check network settings for valid IP address and connectivity. Ping PACS server if tools are available.

steps.title: Confirm DICOM Configuration Settings
steps.instructions: Verify AE Title, PACS IP address, port, and device name match hospital configuration.

steps.title: Perform a Test Send
steps.instructions: Send a test study and confirm it appears in PACS.

steps.title: Check for Network Restrictions
steps.instructions: Verify with IT there are no VLAN, firewall, or port restrictions affecting communication.

steps.title: Restart the System
steps.instructions: Power down completely, wait 30 seconds, and restart the system.

steps.title: Try Alternate Network Port
steps.instructions: Connect to a known working network port to rule out infrastructure issues.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound unable to send studies to PACS; export failing.
CCR.Cause: Incorrect DICOM AE Title configured, preventing communication with PACS server.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected AE Title and verified successful test transmission to PACS.

helpfulDetails: DICOM settings reviewed (AE Title, IP, port)

title: Samsung Healthcare HM70A Ultrasound System - Touchscreen or Control Panel Unresponsive
description: Troubleshooting an unresponsive touchscreen or control panel, including power, lock settings, peripheral issues, and external causes affecting input response.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the system from active patient use before troubleshooting. Move the patient to another ultrasound system if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the system and confirm the touchscreen or control panel is unresponsive. Determine if the entire screen or only certain areas are affected and whether buttons, trackball, or keyboard are also affected.

steps.title: Check for Screen Lock or Freeze Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the system is not in a locked or frozen state. Look for lock icons or inactive UI indicators and attempt to use physical freeze or unlock controls.

steps.title: Perform a System Reboot
steps.instructions: Power down the system completely, wait 15–30 seconds, then restart.

steps.title: Inspect for External Obstructions or Contamination
steps.instructions: Check for gel residue, dirt, debris, or moisture on the touchscreen and control panel. Clean using approved disinfectant wipes.

steps.title: Check Connected Accessories and Peripherals
steps.instructions: Disconnect external devices such as USB devices, keyboards, mice, or network cables to rule out interference.

steps.title: Test Alternate Input Methods
steps.instructions: Attempt to use trackball, physical buttons, or keyboard to determine if some inputs still function.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check for cracked screen, loose or damaged control panel, or signs of impact or wear.

steps.title: Check for System Performance Issues
steps.instructions: Observe if the system is slow, freezing, or lagging prior to becoming unresponsive.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen and control panel not responding during ultrasound exam.
CCR.Cause: Touchscreen remained unresponsive after reboot and cleaning; likely internal digitizer or control interface failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from service, labeled out of service, and sent for vendor repair.

helpfulDetails: Final device status: Removed from service

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: Addresses failed calibration or QC caused by setup, detector condition, positioning, environment, power, test equipment, or persistent system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Use
steps.instructions: If the failed QC test affects confidence in image quality, detector performance, or radiation output, do not return the system to patient use until the failure is understood and resolved. Provide another verified mobile X-ray unit when needed. Expected outcome: A system with unresolved performance concerns is not used clinically.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Test Failed
steps.instructions: Identify the exact calibration or QC procedure, the stage where it failed, the displayed message, and whether the test previously passed. Do not substitute a different test for the failed requirement. Expected outcome: The specific failure is documented and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the approved test object, detector, positioning, orientation, distance, and other setup elements are correct according to the applicable procedure. Do not invent or approximate test geometry. Expected outcome: The calibration or QC procedure is being performed with the correct setup. If setup error caused the failure, repeat the approved test and stop when it passes.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Detector and Imaging Surfaces
steps.instructions: Check the detector and test object for contamination, damage, improper covers, or foreign material that could affect the measurement. Expected outcome: Imaging surfaces and test objects are clean and intact.

steps.title: 5. Confirm System Readiness and Power
steps.instructions: Verify the GM85 Fit has completed startup, the intended detector is ready, battery state is adequate, and no other system warning is active. Expected outcome: The system is stable and ready before the test begins.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for unusual temperature conditions, vibration, direct interference from nearby equipment, unstable flooring, or other obvious environmental changes that could affect testing. Expected outcome: Testing is performed under appropriate and stable environmental conditions.

steps.title: 7. Verify Test Equipment
steps.instructions: If external meters, phantoms, fixtures, or accessories are used, confirm they are the correct equipment and their calibration or verification status is current according to facility policy. Expected outcome: The measurement equipment itself is not the source of the failure.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Approved Test Once Conditions Are Correct
steps.instructions: After correcting any external setup problem, repeat the applicable manufacturer or facility-approved test. Do not repeatedly recalibrate the system in an attempt to force a passing result. Expected outcome: The system passes the required test. If the failure repeats under correct conditions, stop external troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: 9. Document Return-to-Service Evidence
steps.instructions: Record the test performed and passing result according to department policy before releasing the unit. Expected outcome: Objective evidence supports return to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology reported that the GM85 Fit detector quality-control test would not complete successfully.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detector was positioned incorrectly for the approved QC setup.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the detector and test-object positioning, repeated the approved QC procedure successfully, and documented the passing result.

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: Addresses cooling or temperature faults caused by blocked airflow, environmental conditions, contamination, fan obstruction, heavy use, or internal cooling problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Continued Operation
steps.instructions: If the GM85 Fit reports an overtemperature condition, emits unusual heat or odor, or shows signs of cooling failure, stop clinical use. Move required imaging to another verified system. Expected outcome: The system is no longer being operated under a potentially damaging or unsafe thermal condition.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves a temperature warning, fan noise, fan not running, unexpected shutdown, hot enclosure, or repeated fault during heavy use. Record the exact displayed message if present. Expected outcome: The thermal symptom and operating condition are clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Ventilation Openings
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible air inlets and outlets for dust buildup, coverings, bedding, wall contact, or other obstructions. Do not insert tools into ventilation openings or remove internal covers. Expected outcome: Airflow paths are externally clear. If removing an external blockage resolves the condition, continue with controlled verification.

steps.title: 4. Check the Operating Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit is not positioned against heat-producing equipment, in direct sunlight, against a wall that blocks ventilation, or in an unusually hot enclosed area. Expected outcome: The system is operating in a normal clinical environment with unrestricted external ventilation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Excessive Dust or Contamination
steps.instructions: Check accessible vent surfaces for accumulated lint, dust, or debris. Clean only externally and using approved methods. Expected outcome: External vent surfaces are clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Listen for Abnormal Fan Behavior
steps.instructions: During a safe controlled startup, listen for grinding, rubbing, repeated cycling, or absence of expected airflow. Do not operate the system extensively merely to determine whether the fault will recur. Expected outcome: Cooling operation sounds and airflow appear normal. Abnormal fan behavior requires service evaluation.

steps.title: 7. Allow Appropriate Cooling Before Retest
steps.instructions: If the condition followed prolonged use and no damage is present, allow the system to return to a normal temperature before performing a controlled functional check. Do not apply external forced cooling methods not approved for the equipment. Expected outcome: The system restarts without a thermal warning and remains stable under limited verification. Recurring faults require escalation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the system completes startup, remains responsive, provides normal cooling indications, and does not reproduce the fault during appropriate functional testing. Expected outcome: The thermal condition does not recur and the system remains stable. If cooling behavior remains questionable, do not return it to service.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology staff reported that the GM85 Fit displayed an overtemperature warning during bedside use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external ventilation opening obstructed by material stored against the system.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared the obstruction, allowed the system to cool, and verified stable operation without recurrence before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Duration or intensity of prior use

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Addresses detector-not-ready or acquisition problems caused by detector power, charging, pairing, connections, positioning, or communication conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Imaging Availability
steps.instructions: Do not delay necessary imaging while troubleshooting unreliable acquisition hardware. Use another verified detector or mobile X-ray system if clinically required. Do not make repeated patient exposures while attempting to prove whether the detector is functioning. Expected outcome: Patient imaging continuity is maintained without unnecessary exposure. Troubleshooting proceeds without a patient depending on the affected system.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the detector is not detected, appears offline, does not reach ready status, disconnects intermittently, or fails only during acquisition. Record any displayed message exactly as shown. Expected outcome: The failure condition is clearly defined and reproducible. If detector readiness is restored before further action, continue with controlled verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Detector Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the detector externally for cracks, impact damage, loose covers, contamination, fluid exposure, or damaged connector areas. Do not use a detector showing physical damage that could affect electrical safety, image integrity, or internal components. Expected outcome: The detector is externally intact. Visible impact or liquid damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify Detector Power and Charge State
steps.instructions: Confirm the detector is powered as intended and has adequate charge. If charging or docking is used, verify proper seating and normal external charging indications. Compare operation after adequate charging when battery depletion is suspected. Expected outcome: The detector has sufficient power and reaches its normal available state. If charging resolves the problem, verify acquisition functionality and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check Detector Selection and Association
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended detector is selected or associated with the system using normal operator-accessible controls. If multiple detectors are used in the department, confirm staff have not selected or brought the wrong detector to the system. Do not enter restricted service configuration menus. Expected outcome: The correct detector is selected and recognized. If correcting detector selection restores readiness, complete functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Wireless and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: If detector communication is wireless, confirm the detector is within the expected operating area and that obvious environmental or infrastructure changes have not occurred. Compare behavior near the system versus farther away. Avoid changing network infrastructure without coordination. Expected outcome: Detector communication remains stable under normal operating conditions. If location or external interference is clearly responsible, document and escalate infrastructure concerns as appropriate.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Detector Connections
steps.instructions: Where a wired connection, charger, docking location, or external accessory is involved, inspect the connection for bent contacts, contamination, loose seating, or damage. Use only approved cleaning methods and accessories. Expected outcome: Accessible detector interfaces are clean, intact, and securely connected. If correcting an external connection restores readiness, stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good Detector When Approved
steps.instructions: If another compatible, approved detector is available and department procedures permit substitution, test the system with the known-good detector. Do not change system configuration beyond normal supported detector selection. Expected outcome: A known-good detector either operates normally, isolating the issue to the original detector, or shows the same problem, suggesting a system or communication issue.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Acquisition Verification
steps.instructions: Use the approved facility or manufacturer method for nonpatient operational verification. Confirm the detector reaches ready status, remains connected, and produces a usable image without communication interruption. Expected outcome: Detector status and acquisition remain stable. If so, the system may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology staff reported that the GM85 Fit detector remained unavailable and the system would not become ready for acquisition.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detector battery discharged and the detector was not fully seated in its charging location.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering correctly seated and charged the detector, confirmed stable recognition and acquisition readiness, and completed functional verification.

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Addresses failed worklist retrieval or image transfer caused by network connection, destination availability, configuration, selection, or infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Workflow and Patient Identification
steps.instructions: Do not allow a network problem to result in incorrect patient selection or study association. Use the facility-approved downtime workflow when worklist or PACS connectivity is unavailable. Expected outcome: Patient identification and imaging continuity are maintained safely despite the communication failure.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects modality worklist, image transfer to PACS, DICOM storage confirmation, query functions, or all network communication. Record any displayed message and whether previously acquired images remain stored locally. Expected outcome: The failed service is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Check Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the Ethernet cable, connector, and wall connection if the system is using wired networking. If wireless networking is used, verify that the system indicates an expected connection without changing protected configuration. Expected outcome: The basic network connection is physically present and stable. If restoring a disconnected cable resolves communication, verify transfer and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Compare With Other Network Functions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the GM85 Fit can communicate with any configured network destination or whether all network functions are unavailable. Where practical, compare with another device in the same clinical area to determine whether an infrastructure outage may be present. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the mobile X-ray system, a specific destination, or the broader hospital network.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Intended Destination
steps.instructions: Using normal operator-accessible information, confirm staff are attempting to send to the expected PACS or retrieve from the intended worklist source. Do not edit AE titles, IP addresses, ports, or other protected DICOM parameters without authorization. Expected outcome: The correct destination is selected.

steps.title: 6. Check for Pending or Unsent Studies
steps.instructions: Review the normal study or transfer status interface for queued, failed, or pending exams. Do not delete unsent patient studies as a troubleshooting shortcut. Expected outcome: Stored studies remain identifiable and available for transfer once communication is restored.

steps.title: 7. Coordinate Infrastructure Verification
steps.instructions: If physical connectivity appears normal but communication remains unavailable, coordinate with hospital IT, PACS, or network support to verify destination availability, network path, VLAN access, and related infrastructure. Provide the device identification and observed symptoms without independently changing enterprise network settings. Expected outcome: Infrastructure is either confirmed functional or a network-side issue is identified.

steps.title: 8. Retry the Transfer or Worklist Query
steps.instructions: Once connectivity is restored or an external issue is corrected, retry the failed communication using normal system functions. Expected outcome: Worklist data is retrieved or images transfer successfully with expected acknowledgment.

steps.title: 9. Verify End-to-End Clinical Communication
steps.instructions: Confirm not only that the system reports a successful send, but that the intended study appears correctly at the receiving PACS or other destination when verification is available. Expected outcome: The complete communication path is functional. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology reported that the GM85 Fit acquired images normally but could not send studies to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the Ethernet cable disconnected from the assigned network connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the network connection, resent the queued study, and verified successful receipt at the PACS destination.

helpfulDetails: Whether worklist, PACS transfer, or both failed

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Addresses exposures that will not initiate or abort because of readiness, detector, control, interlock, connection, power, or acquisition conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Unnecessary Exposure
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt patient exposures while troubleshooting. If clinically necessary imaging cannot be completed promptly, move the examination to another verified system. Expected outcome: No unnecessary radiation exposure occurs while the failure is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system never reaches ready status, the exposure control does nothing, an exposure starts and aborts, or the system returns a message. Record the exact displayed message and circumstances. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly categorized. If the condition cannot be reproduced, continue checking for intermittent external causes before returning to service.

steps.title: 3. Confirm System and Detector Readiness
steps.instructions: Verify the console shows the system and intended detector in the expected ready state. Resolve detector-not-ready conditions before troubleshooting exposure generation itself. Expected outcome: Detector and acquisition systems are available. If correcting detector readiness restores exposures, complete functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check Exposure Controls and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the hand switch, exposure control, cable, connector, and accessible strain relief for damage, looseness, sticking, or contamination. Confirm the control is connected as intended. Do not bypass or jumper exposure-control circuits. Expected outcome: The exposure control is intact, connected, and responds normally. If reseating a loose approved connection restores operation, verify and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify System Position and Operating State
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is not in transport, shutdown, charging-only, error, or another operating state that prevents exposure. Verify any normal operator-accessible preparation steps are complete without changing protected configuration. Expected outcome: The system enters the expected acquisition-ready state.

steps.title: 6. Verify Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm sufficient battery state and stable system power. If the unit behaves differently while connected to a verified AC source, document the difference. Expected outcome: Exposure operation is not being prevented by an inadequate system power condition. If restoring the proper power state corrects the issue, complete final verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for External Damage or Recent Events
steps.instructions: Ask whether the unit was dropped, collided with equipment, exposed to fluid, abruptly powered down, or moved immediately before the problem occurred. Inspect accessible exterior areas for signs of impact. Expected outcome: No external event suggests unsafe internal damage. If significant impact or liquid intrusion is identified, remove the system from service.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Nonpatient Exposure Test
steps.instructions: Using facility-approved procedures, an appropriate test object, and required radiation-safety precautions, perform a controlled functional exposure test. Do not use a patient to confirm whether an intermittent system problem remains. Expected outcome: The exposure initiates, completes without aborting, and produces the expected acquisition result. If so, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Repeatability
steps.instructions: Where appropriate, repeat the approved functional test sufficiently to establish that the problem is not intermittent. Expected outcome: Exposure initiation and completion remain reliable. Intermittent exposure operation requires removal from service even if one test succeeds.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology staff reported that the GM85 Fit reached the bedside but would not initiate an exposure.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external exposure hand-switch connector partially disengaged.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering securely reconnected the exposure control, completed approved nonpatient exposure testing, and verified reliable operation before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Recent collision, drop, or fluid exposure
Whether the exposure never started or aborted

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Gantry, Table, or Positioning Motion Is Unavailable
description: Addresses unavailable system movement or positioning caused by locks, obstructions, controls, battery state, mechanical interference, or positioning-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Unintended Movement
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot positioning or powered movement while the system is positioned against a patient, bed, or other equipment. Move the patient or substitute another verified imaging system when necessary. Secure the GM85 Fit so unexpected movement cannot cause injury or collision. Expected outcome: The system is safely separated from the patient and surrounding equipment. If movement is unpredictable or unsafe, remove the unit from service immediately.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Motion Is Unavailable
steps.instructions: Identify whether the complaint involves mobile drive movement, tube-column positioning, arm movement, detector positioning, braking, steering, or another specific positioning function. Attempt only safe unloaded movement while observing indicators and displayed messages. Expected outcome: The affected motion is clearly identified and the failure can be reproduced. If all movement operates normally, inspect for an intermittent or environment-related condition before release.

steps.title: 3. Check for Physical Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect around wheels, casters, column, tube assembly, handles, detector storage areas, cables, bedding, wall fixtures, and nearby equipment. Remove only external obstructions that can be safely cleared. Expected outcome: The travel path and movable structures are unobstructed. If removing an obstruction restores normal movement, verify the full safe operating range and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Verify Brakes, Locks, and Positioning Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm that brakes, mechanical locks, transport locks, or other normal positioning restraints are not engaged when movement is expected. Check that operator controls return normally and are not physically stuck or damaged. Expected outcome: Required locks and brakes respond normally and movement becomes available when properly released. If motion returns, complete functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify System Power and Battery State
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is fully powered and not in a shutdown, low-power, charging-only, or fault condition that limits movement. If powered movement depends on battery operation, verify adequate charge indication and compare behavior under verified AC or charged conditions when appropriate. Expected outcome: The system has sufficient power for normal movement. If normal movement returns after restoring an appropriate power state, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Handles and Drive Controls
steps.instructions: For powered transport functions, inspect accessible drive handles, switches, sensors, or controls for contamination, physical damage, sticking, or abnormal feel. Do not disassemble handle assemblies or bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: External drive controls appear intact and respond consistently. If cleaning an externally contaminated control or correcting an obvious external condition restores movement, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check Mechanical Condition
steps.instructions: Observe wheels, casters, column travel, tube assembly, and accessible moving structures for binding, unusual resistance, looseness, abnormal noise, or evidence of impact. Do not force movement through resistance. Expected outcome: Mechanical movement is smooth and free of obvious external damage. Binding, grinding, or structural damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Verify Positioning After Correction
steps.instructions: Move the system through the clinically required range without a patient. Confirm brakes hold when applied, the unit stops predictably, steering is controllable, and the tube assembly remains secure when positioned. Expected outcome: All required positioning functions operate smoothly and safely. If they do, the system may be returned to service after required verification.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GM85 Fit could not be moved normally between bedside locations.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external cable lodged near a caster and restricting system movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared the obstruction, inspected the caster area, verified smooth transport and braking, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether movement was powered or manual
Any evidence of collision or impact

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Image Quality Is Poor or Artifacts Are Present
description: Addresses poor images or artifacts caused by detector condition, positioning, technique, contamination, processing, movement, or environmental factors.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Repeat Exposure
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly expose a patient while investigating image quality. If diagnostic images cannot be obtained reliably, use another verified system. Retain representative problem images when allowed by facility procedure. Expected outcome: Repeat radiation exposure is minimized and evidence of the reported artifact is preserved.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Image Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves lines, bands, spots, nonuniformity, clipping, excessive noise, blur, incorrect brightness, missing image areas, or a recurring location-specific artifact. Determine whether the issue affects all studies, one detector, one exam type, or one location. Expected outcome: The artifact is consistently described and narrowed to a useful pattern.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Detector Surface
steps.instructions: Inspect the detector for contamination, adhesive residue, fluid, protective-cover damage, impact damage, or foreign material. Clean only according to approved methods. Expected outcome: The detector surface is clean and undamaged. If removal of external contamination eliminates the artifact during approved verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Positioning and External Objects
steps.instructions: Review the imaging setup for bedding, monitoring leads, jewelry, support devices, grid misalignment, detector covers, or other objects that could appear in the image. Expected outcome: No unintended objects or positioning problems are present in the imaging field. If correcting setup removes the artifact, verify and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Technique and Exam Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected exam and technique settings are appropriate for the intended test condition without altering protected protocols. Compare the reported problem with another equivalent study or test image when available. Expected outcome: Poor quality is not explained by an incorrect exam selection or obvious operator-accessible setting.

steps.title: 6. Check for Motion-Related Blur
steps.instructions: If images are blurred, evaluate whether patient motion, detector movement, tube movement, or instability of the mobile unit could explain the finding. Check brakes and positioning stability. Expected outcome: The system remains mechanically stable during image acquisition. If stability correction eliminates the problem, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Detector When Available
steps.instructions: If multiple compatible detectors are approved for the system, compare image quality using a known-good detector and an appropriate test object. Expected outcome: The artifact follows the original detector or remains with the system, helping isolate the source without unnecessary disassembly.

steps.title: 8. Review Calibration or Correction Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that required operator-accessible calibration or quality-control functions are current and successfully completed according to approved facility and manufacturer procedures. Do not initiate undocumented service calibrations. Expected outcome: Required quality-control functions pass. A failed calibration should be addressed as a calibration or service issue rather than masked by repeated patient imaging.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Image-Quality Verification
steps.instructions: Use an approved test object or phantom and the appropriate facility procedure to evaluate image consistency after correction. Expected outcome: Test images are free of the reported artifact and meet applicable acceptance criteria. If so, the system may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology staff reported a recurring linear artifact on images acquired with the GM85 Fit.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found residue on the detector surface in the same location as the reported artifact.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the detector using the approved method, performed test imaging, and verified the artifact was no longer present before returning the detector to service.

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Addresses studies that cannot save, process, reconstruct, or export because of storage, workflow, network, software, or study-state problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data and Avoid Repeat Exposure
steps.instructions: Do not repeat a patient exposure simply because a completed image will not save or export. Preserve the current study and locally stored images whenever possible. Use another verified system for additional imaging if necessary. Expected outcome: Existing patient data is protected and unnecessary radiation exposure is avoided.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Workflow Step Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the image is acquired but will not save locally, processing does not complete, the study remains pending, reconstruction fails, or export to PACS or external media fails. Record any displayed message exactly. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to a specific part of the workflow.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Study Is Complete and Valid
steps.instructions: Using normal operator-accessible functions, confirm the study has required patient identification and is not still in an incomplete acquisition state. Do not alter clinical demographics solely to bypass a save problem. Expected outcome: The study is in a valid state for normal saving or export.

steps.title: 4. Check Local System Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Confirm the console remains responsive and other studies or normal functions can be viewed. If the workstation is frozen or unstable, address the workstation condition before assuming a storage-specific problem. Expected outcome: The local workstation is operating normally or the issue is recognized as a broader system fault.

steps.title: 5. Check Storage or Queue Status
steps.instructions: Review normal system indicators for storage warnings, pending studies, transfer queues, or failed exports. Do not delete clinical studies or clear queues simply to free space unless authorized procedures specifically direct it and patient data has been protected. Expected outcome: Any visible storage or queue condition is identified without risking patient data.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether Saving and Export Are Separate
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the study exists locally but cannot export, or whether it never saves locally. A study that saves locally but will not transmit points toward communication or destination issues rather than image acquisition. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to local storage, processing, or downstream transfer.

steps.title: 7. Verify Destination Connectivity
steps.instructions: If export is the only failure, check physical network connectivity, the selected destination, and whether other studies can transfer. Coordinate with PACS or IT if the destination appears unavailable. Expected outcome: The export path is either restored or ruled out as the source of the problem.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart Only After Protecting Data
steps.instructions: If the application remains unstable and locally acquired patient data is protected according to facility procedure, perform a normal supported restart when appropriate. Avoid hard shutdowns when unsaved patient data may still be recoverable. Expected outcome: The system returns to stable operation without loss of required patient information.

steps.title: 9. Verify With a Nonpatient Test Workflow
steps.instructions: After correction, use an approved test or nonpatient workflow to confirm acquisition, processing, local saving, and export functions. Expected outcome: A complete test workflow saves and processes correctly, and export succeeds when required. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology reported that images acquired on the GM85 Fit remained on the system and would not export to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network connection disconnected while local study storage remained functional.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored network connectivity, successfully transferred the pending study to PACS, and verified a complete test save-and-export workflow.

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Addresses no-power, incomplete startup, or boot problems caused by charging, power, connections, controls, battery state, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Imaging Availability
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the GM85 Fit while it is required for an active patient procedure. Move clinical imaging to another verified mobile X-ray system if imaging is urgently needed. Inspect for smoke, unusual odor, excessive heat, liquid intrusion, damaged power components, or evidence of impact. If any are present, disconnect from AC power when safe and remove the system from service. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by alternate equipment and the GM85 Fit is safe for controlled troubleshooting. If a physical or electrical hazard is present, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Determine exactly what staff observed: completely dead system, display remaining blank, indicators illuminating without completing startup, unexpected shutdown during boot, or repeated restart. Attempt one controlled startup while observing display activity, indicator lights, audible sounds, and any displayed message. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced and clearly defined. If the unit starts normally and remains stable, continue with functional verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Charging Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the AC cord is fully seated and undamaged. Inspect the plug, cord, strain relief, and accessible connector surfaces. Verify the wall outlet using an approved electrical tester or known-good equipment when appropriate. Avoid relying solely on the presence of a receptacle. Expected outcome: The unit is connected to a verified power source and responds appropriately to AC connection. If normal startup is restored, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check External Power and Emergency Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible power switches, shutdown controls, emergency-stop or safety controls if applicable to the installed configuration, and confirm none are inadvertently activated or physically damaged. Do not bypass safety controls. Expected outcome: All external controls required for normal startup are in their operating condition. If resetting a legitimately activated external control restores operation, verify normal startup and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Evaluate Battery Condition
steps.instructions: If the system can operate from battery, compare behavior on verified AC power and battery operation. Observe whether battery or charging indicators appear abnormal. A severely depleted or degraded battery may prevent expected startup or mobile operation even when other components appear functional. Expected outcome: The system either starts normally from an appropriate power condition or the problem is isolated to battery-related operation. If stable operation is restored after adequate charging or an approved known-good battery-related correction, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Accessible Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible connections associated with the operator console, display, detector charging or docking functions, and other user-accessible modules. Reseat only connections intended for normal external connection and service access. Do not open covers or disturb internal wiring. Expected outcome: Connections are secure and undamaged. If a loose external connection was responsible and startup completes normally after correction, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Perform One Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If no hazard is present and the manufacturer-supported operating sequence permits it, perform a normal shutdown or power cycle rather than repeatedly forcing restarts. Allow the system to complete its startup sequence without unnecessary control inputs. Expected outcome: The GM85 Fit completes startup and reaches its normal ready state. If it repeatedly freezes, restarts, or fails at the same point, remove it from service and escalate.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the console remains responsive, system status is normal, battery and charging behavior are reasonable, detector communication is available, and the unit can be positioned safely. Perform appropriate operational testing before clinical release. Do not make a patient exposure solely for troubleshooting unless permitted by facility procedures and appropriate test methods. Expected outcome: The system starts consistently and all required functions operate normally. The unit may be returned to service when required verification is complete.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Samsung GM85 Fit would not complete startup and remained unavailable for imaging.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the system connected to a wall outlet that was not supplying power, leaving the battery discharged.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering connected the unit to a verified powered outlet, confirmed charging and successful startup, and completed functional verification before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of damage, heat, odor, or liquid exposure

title: Samsung Healthcare GM85 Fit Mobile X-Ray System - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Addresses console freezes or communication loss involving the detector, acquisition system, display, network, or connected system components.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Completed Work
steps.instructions: If the workstation freezes during a patient examination, stop further exposures until system status is known. If images have already been acquired, avoid unnecessary restart actions that could risk unsaved data when another safe recovery method is available. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on an unstable workstation and available study data is preserved when possible.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Failure Scope
steps.instructions: Determine whether only the display is unresponsive, the full workstation is frozen, the detector disconnected, network communication stopped, or the entire system restarted. Record any message and the workflow step where the problem occurred. Expected outcome: The affected communication path is identified.

steps.title: 3. Check Basic Console Response
steps.instructions: Test normal user-accessible controls without rapidly repeating commands. Observe whether the cursor, touchscreen, keyboard, or other controls respond. Expected outcome: The console either recovers normally or remains unresponsive. Persistent freezing requires further isolation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible console, display, detector, docking, and network connections for looseness or damage. Reseat only connections designed for normal external access. Expected outcome: All accessible connections are secure. If a loose external connection caused the problem and stable operation returns, complete verification.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Network-Related
steps.instructions: Check whether local acquisition functions operate while network functions fail. If detector communication is also lost, determine whether the problem involves only the detector or multiple system functions. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to the local workstation, detector communication, or network infrastructure.

steps.title: 6. Verify Network Link Indications
steps.instructions: Where accessible, inspect Ethernet connections and link indicators. Confirm the correct network cable and wall connection are being used. Do not alter IP addressing, VLANs, routing, or protected network settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Physical network connectivity is present when network communication is expected.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the workstation remains frozen and patient care is no longer dependent on it, use the normal manufacturer-supported restart or shutdown process when possible. Avoid repeated hard power interruptions. Expected outcome: The system returns to normal operation and reconnects to required devices. Repeated freezing or communication loss is not acceptable for return to service.

steps.title: 8. Verify Acquisition and Communication
steps.instructions: After recovery, confirm the intended detector connects, console controls remain responsive, images can be acquired using an approved test method, and required network functions are available. Expected outcome: Operation remains stable without freezing or dropped communication. If stable, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Radiology staff reported that the GM85 Fit console froze and stopped responding during exam preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external network connector partially disengaged after the unit had been moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the network connection, performed a controlled restart, and verified stable console, detector, and network operation before release.

title: Samsung Healthcare V8 Ultrasound System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed ultrasound calibration or quality-control checks caused by setup, probes, test equipment, configuration, environment, or persistent system performance problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Determine Clinical Impact
steps.instructions: If the failed QC or calibration test calls imaging accuracy or performance into question, do not use the affected V8 or probe for clinical imaging until the failure is understood and resolved. Provide another verified ultrasound system when necessary. Expected outcome: Clinical imaging does not continue on equipment with unverified performance.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Test That Failed
steps.instructions: Record: Name of the calibration or QC test Probe used Test equipment or phantom used Exact failure message or observed abnormality Whether the test previously passed Whether the problem is repeatable Whether one or multiple probes are affected Do not substitute an invented acceptance criterion if the approved procedure is unavailable. Expected outcome: The failed test is clearly identified and can be repeated under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Test Procedure and Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the test is being performed according to the applicable manufacturer, organizational, or approved QC procedure. Check: Correct probe Correct test object or phantom Correct setup and positioning Correct imaging mode Correct approved configuration Appropriate coupling Stable test environment Expected outcome: The test setup matches the approved procedure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Probe and Connections
steps.instructions: Examine the probe, cable, strain relief, and connector for damage. Reseat the probe connection when appropriate. A damaged or intermittent probe can produce a QC failure without an internal system fault. Expected outcome: Probe integrity and connection are verified, or a defective probe is isolated.

steps.title: 5. Verify Test Equipment Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the QC phantom, test fixture, cables, sensors, or other test equipment used. Confirm it is the appropriate equipment for the procedure and that its condition or calibration status is acceptable under your department's program. Expected outcome: Test equipment is suitable and not responsible for an invalid failure.

steps.title: 6. Repeat the Test Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Repeat the approved test after correcting any setup, connection, or environmental issue. Do not repeatedly adjust calibration merely to force a passing result. Expected outcome: The test passes consistently. If it does, document the identified cause, complete required verification, and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Probe When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the failed test is probe-dependent, repeat the relevant approved QC check using a known-good compatible probe if the procedure permits. Expected outcome: The comparison isolates the failure to the original probe or demonstrates a broader system problem.

steps.title: 8. Review Accessible Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that normal user-accessible or department-approved configuration has not been unintentionally changed. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or alter calibration coefficients without manufacturer-approved service procedures. Expected outcome: No inappropriate accessible configuration is contributing to the failure.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Repeatability
steps.instructions: A single anomalous result can arise from poor setup or test conditions. A repeated failure under controlled conditions is more significant. Repeat only as permitted by the approved procedure and document the results. Expected outcome: The test either passes reproducibly or demonstrates a consistent failure requiring escalation.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated QC or Calibration Failure
steps.instructions: If the V8 or probe repeatedly fails an approved QC or calibration test after external factors are ruled out, remove the affected equipment from service. Do not perform unauthorized internal calibration or board-level repair. Expected outcome: Equipment with unverified performance is escalated for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that a routine image-quality QC check on the Samsung V8 failed when performed with one probe.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the failure followed the reported probe while the same approved QC setup passed with a known-good compatible probe.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected probe from service, repeated the approved QC check successfully with the known-good probe, and returned the V8 to service.

title: Samsung Healthcare V8 Ultrasound System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: Troubleshoots overheating warnings, abnormal fan behavior, blocked ventilation, excessive heat, and environmental conditions affecting Samsung V8 cooling.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Respond to Heat Safely
steps.instructions: If the V8 displays an overtemperature condition, becomes unusually hot, emits an abnormal odor, or shows signs of thermal damage, discontinue clinical use. Move the examination to another verified ultrasound system and shut down the V8 normally if safe to do so. If smoke or evidence of electrical burning is present, disconnect power if safe and follow facility safety procedures. Expected outcome: The patient and staff are no longer exposed to equipment with a possible thermal fault.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Thermal Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether staff observed: An overtemperature message Fan noise No audible fan activity where normally expected Excessive exterior heat Shutdown during prolonged use Restart after cooling Heat only in a particular room or location Record any message exactly. Expected outcome: The thermal symptom and operating conditions are clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Ventilation Openings
steps.instructions: With the system safely powered down when appropriate, inspect accessible ventilation areas for: Dust accumulation Paper or fabric blocking airflow Equipment positioned directly against a wall or cabinet Accessories obstructing vents External contamination Clean only accessible areas using approved methods. Do not open covers merely to clean internal fans. Expected outcome: External airflow paths are unobstructed.

steps.title: 4. Check the Environment
steps.instructions: Verify that the system is not operating in an obviously abnormal environment such as: Directly beside a heat-producing device In direct sunlight In a confined space with poor airflow Near a blocked HVAC supply or return In an unusually warm room Do not invent acceptable temperature limits without approved documentation. Expected outcome: The environment is suitable for normal equipment operation.

steps.title: 5. Check External Fan Behavior
steps.instructions: During a controlled startup or functional test, observe accessible fan noise and airflow behavior without inserting objects into vents. Listen for: Grinding Rattling Repeated speed changes No apparent airflow when the system indicates a cooling problem Expected outcome: No obvious external evidence of fan obstruction or mechanical fan failure is present.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Dust and Contamination
steps.instructions: Check external vents and accessible filters only where inspection or servicing is permitted by approved procedures. Do not remove internal assemblies or improvise cleaning methods. Expected outcome: Accessible cooling surfaces are clean enough for normal airflow or are serviced according to approved procedures.

steps.title: 7. Remove Heat-Producing External Conditions
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential peripherals if they are physically obstructing ventilation or contributing to abnormal operating conditions. Reposition the system appropriately and allow it to return to a normal condition before retesting. Expected outcome: The system operates without renewed temperature warnings after the external condition is corrected.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Functional Test
steps.instructions: After the system has cooled and external airflow issues are corrected: Start the V8 normally Verify the display and controls Confirm probe recognition Perform a reasonable functional imaging test Monitor for recurring thermal warnings or abnormal fan behavior Do not intentionally stress the system beyond approved service testing. Expected outcome: The system operates normally without heat warnings or abnormal cooling behavior. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Recurring Thermal or Fan Problems
steps.instructions: If the overtemperature condition recurs, the fan makes abnormal mechanical noise, the unit shuts down from heat, or the enclosure remains unusually hot, discontinue use. Do not bypass temperature monitoring or perform internal fan or power-supply repair without appropriate service procedures. Expected outcome: The V8 is removed from service for qualified thermal-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Samsung V8 became unusually warm and displayed a temperature-related warning during use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that stored accessories were blocking an external ventilation area and restricting airflow.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the obstruction, repositioned the accessories, allowed the system to cool, verified stable imaging operation without recurrence of the warning, and returned the V8 to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the fault occurred after prolonged use
Whether the fault recurred after cooling

title: Samsung Healthcare V8 Ultrasound System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Troubleshoots probes or acquisition hardware that are not recognized, unavailable, intermittently detected, or unable to become ready for imaging.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Imaging Capability
steps.instructions: Do not continue a clinical examination using an intermittently recognized or unreliable probe. Move the patient to another verified system or use another appropriate verified probe when clinically acceptable. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on unreliable acquisition hardware.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Not-Ready Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: No probe detected Probe shown but unavailable Intermittent recognition Acquisition controls unavailable A specific probe only Multiple probes Loss of readiness after moving the system or cable Record any displayed message exactly as observed. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to a particular probe, port, accessory, or system-wide acquisition condition.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Probe and Cable
steps.instructions: Remove the affected probe from clinical use long enough to inspect: Probe housing Acoustic lens or scanning surface Cable Strain relief Connector body Connector pins or contacts that are safely visible Evidence of cuts, crushing, fluid intrusion, or impact Do not use a damaged probe on a patient. Expected outcome: The probe and cable are externally intact, or damaged hardware is identified and removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Reseat the Probe Connection
steps.instructions: With the system in an appropriate state for connecting or disconnecting probes according to approved operating practices, fully disconnect and reconnect the affected probe. Make sure the connector is correctly aligned, fully seated, and secured using the normal connector mechanism. Do not force a connector. Expected outcome: The probe is recognized and becomes available for imaging. If recognition remains stable, proceed to verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe Port Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible probe connection area for contamination, foreign material, damage, or signs that the connector is not seating normally. Do not insert tools into the connector or attempt contact repair without authorized procedures. Expected outcome: The port is externally clean, undamaged, and able to accept the probe connection normally.

steps.title: 6. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: If available, connect a known-good compatible probe using approved handling practices. Compare the result: If the known-good probe works on the same connection, suspect the original probe or its cable. If multiple verified probes fail at the same connection, the problem may involve the port or system. If the original probe works reliably on another approved connection, investigate the original connection path. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the probe, connection path, or system without opening the equipment.

steps.title: 7. Check Selected Probe and Exam Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that the intended probe is selected and that the system is operating in an appropriate supported exam or imaging configuration. Do not change protected configurations or enter unauthorized service menus. Expected outcome: The connected probe is correctly selected and available for the intended supported imaging function.

steps.title: 8. Check External Acquisition Accessories
steps.instructions: If the reported problem involves an external accessory or acquisition-related peripheral, inspect its external connection, cable, power state, and compatibility with the intended workflow. Reseat accessible connections and substitute known-good accessories when appropriate. Expected outcome: Required external acquisition hardware is connected, recognized, and stable.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved testing practices: Confirm stable probe recognition Acquire a test image Manipulate the probe cable gently through normal use positions Confirm acquisition remains available Verify no intermittent disconnect occurs Expected outcome: Acquisition hardware remains ready and imaging is stable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Acquisition Hardware Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good compatible probes remain unrecognized or multiple acquisition connections are unreliable, stop external troubleshooting. Do not attempt board-level connector, acquisition-module, or internal electronics repair. Expected outcome: The system or affected probe is appropriately removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that one ultrasound probe was intermittently unavailable on the Samsung V8.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found damage at the probe cable strain relief and reproduced intermittent probe recognition.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged probe from service, verified a known-good compatible probe remained stable on the V8, and returned the ultrasound system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or multiple probes were affected
Whether the problem changes with cable position
Final status of system and probe

title: Samsung Healthcare V8 Ultrasound System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed worklist queries, DICOM transfers, PACS communication, and external network or destination conditions affecting Samsung V8 connectivity.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Workflow and Preserve Images
steps.instructions: Do not delete locally stored patient images or repeatedly resend studies without understanding the transfer status. If clinical interpretation is time-sensitive, follow the facility's approved alternate workflow while troubleshooting communication. Expected outcome: Patient data is preserved and clinical care continues despite the connectivity problem.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Worklist not populating One patient or all patients Images not sending Transfer remaining queued PACS destination unavailable DICOM verification failure Communication lost after a move or network change One destination versus all configured destinations Record the exact displayed message and affected workflow. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to worklist retrieval, image transfer, a specific destination, or general network connectivity.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Ultrasound Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the V8 itself is functioning normally: System is responsive Patient/exam workflow opens Images can be acquired Images can be stored locally A DICOM problem should be separated from a broader workstation failure. Expected outcome: Local imaging and storage operate normally, allowing communication troubleshooting to continue.

steps.title: 4. Check the Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the Ethernet cable and accessible connector. Verify the cable is fully seated and undamaged. If appropriate, test with a known-good approved network cable or confirm the wall port through established IT procedures. Expected outcome: A reliable physical network connection is present.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Network Location Is Functional
steps.instructions: Ask whether: Other networked medical devices in the area are affected The V8 was recently moved The wall jack changed Network maintenance or an outage occurred The problem began after an infrastructure change Coordinate with IT when the evidence points to the network rather than the ultrasound. Expected outcome: Facility network availability is confirmed or an infrastructure issue is identified.

steps.title: 6. Verify Approved Communication Configuration
steps.instructions: Review only accessible, authorized communication information required for troubleshooting, such as the intended destination or network status. Do not alter IP settings, DICOM application identifiers, ports, routing, VLANs, or protected configuration unless authorized and using approved documentation. Compare with documented known-good configuration when available. Expected outcome: The V8 is using the intended approved configuration or a configuration discrepancy is referred to qualified support.

steps.title: 7. Test Worklist Separately From Image Transfer
steps.instructions: Where permitted, perform a controlled test of the affected function. For example: Query the approved worklist Send an approved test study Test another configured destination if one is legitimately available Keep worklist and image-transfer troubleshooting separate because they may use different server paths or services. Expected outcome: The specific failing communication service is identified.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Receiving System
steps.instructions: Coordinate with PACS, radiology IT, or enterprise IT to confirm: The destination is online The service is accepting connections The V8 is recognized as an authorized sender No relevant network or server change occurred The test record was received Expected outcome: The remote side is confirmed operational or the issue is assigned to the appropriate infrastructure team.

steps.title: 9. Retry the Original Workflow After Correction
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cable, network, destination, or approved configuration problem, repeat the affected workflow. Confirm that queued data is handled according to facility procedure and that duplicate records are not unintentionally created. Expected outcome: Worklist retrieval or DICOM transfer succeeds consistently. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Connectivity Failure
steps.instructions: If the V8 operates locally but cannot communicate despite confirmed physical connectivity and verified infrastructure, escalate to Samsung Healthcare technical support and/or the appropriate IT/PACS team. Do not alter protected networking or DICOM parameters by trial and error. Expected outcome: The unresolved communication problem is routed to the correct technical owner.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Samsung V8 could acquire images but would not send completed studies to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the Ethernet cable at the ultrasound was not fully seated and network connectivity was intermittent.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and secured the network cable, sent an approved test study, confirmed receipt with the PACS workflow, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact DICOM or worklist function affected
Whether the unit was recently moved

title: Samsung Healthcare V8 Ultrasound System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Troubleshoots ultrasound acquisition that will not begin, freezes, stops unexpectedly, or is interrupted by probe, control, workflow, or system conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt an unreliable examination while patient care depends on the V8. If acquisition will not remain stable, move the examination to another verified ultrasound system. Expected outcome: Clinical care continues without depending on unreliable acquisition.

steps.title: 2. Clarify What “Will Not Start” or “Aborts” Means
steps.instructions: Ultrasound systems do not normally initiate an X-ray-style exposure. Determine whether staff mean that: Live imaging does not begin Imaging freezes unexpectedly A selected mode will not activate Acquisition stops when a specific probe is used A clip or image capture aborts The system returns to another screen The application freezes during scanning Reproduce the condition using approved testing rather than patient imaging when possible. Expected outcome: The exact acquisition failure is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Probe Recognition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the intended probe is securely connected, recognized by the system, and selectable. Inspect the probe and cable externally and reseat the connection if appropriate. Expected outcome: The probe remains recognized and available. If acquisition begins normally after correcting the probe connection, verify stable operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Verify Exam and Imaging Mode Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm that an appropriate exam type and supported imaging mode are selected for the connected probe. Check that the system is not unintentionally in a frozen, review, measurement, or other state that prevents live acquisition. Expected outcome: The system is configured for live acquisition and responds normally to imaging controls.

steps.title: 5. Check Controls for Normal Operation
steps.instructions: Operate the relevant accessible controls, including freeze/unfreeze and imaging-mode controls, and confirm the user interface responds consistently. Look for a stuck, damaged, or physically obstructed control. Expected outcome: Controls respond predictably and live imaging can be started and stopped normally.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Devices
steps.instructions: If the problem began after connecting a USB device, printer, network peripheral, or other accessory, disconnect nonessential external devices following normal shutdown or connection practices. Repeat the acquisition test. Expected outcome: Imaging remains stable without interference from an external peripheral.

steps.title: 7. Test a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: If the issue appears probe-specific, use a known-good compatible probe. Compare whether acquisition starts and remains stable. Expected outcome: A known-good probe either confirms normal system operation or demonstrates that the problem is system-wide.

steps.title: 8. Check System Responsiveness and Available Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that the V8 is not exhibiting broader signs of software instability such as: Delayed control response Repeated freezing Interface lag Failed patient selection Inability to save images Communication errors occurring at the same time If appropriate, perform a normal controlled restart. Expected outcome: The system responds normally and acquisition remains active after restart.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved testing practices: Start live imaging Freeze and unfreeze normally Change an appropriate imaging mode if relevant Capture a test image or clip Confirm acquisition does not unexpectedly stop Confirm the probe remains recognized Expected outcome: Acquisition starts, remains stable, and completes normally. Troubleshooting can stop.
